people.name: Gisaja
people.title: artist
people.look: A statuesque figure with sea-green eyes, swept obsidian horns and ember-lit eyes, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries a case of pigments and silverpoint styluses and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Kenwunmi
people.title: prophet
people.look: A weather-beaten figure with bright gold eyes, side-whiskers and laugh-lines around bright eyes, and a burn-mark from an old forge spark. Carries ash-streaked robes and a铜 bell and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

people.name: Kumsarluma
people.title: prophet
people.look: A sinewy figure with amber eyes, swept-back silver-blond tresses and long tapered ears, and stern, deeply etched brow lines. Carries a staff hung with scripture-strips and squints thoughtfully before every reply.

people.name: Lingaji
people.title: magician
people.look: A wiry figure with slate-grey eyes, swept obsidian horns and ember-lit eyes, and a faded duelling scar across the cheek. Carries a bandolier of glass phials and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Tupali
people.title: prophet
people.look: A stocky figure with storm-grey eyes, asymmetric crown-horns and warp-etched skin, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries a staff hung with scripture-strips and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Risa
people.title: Angakkuq of Pajalara
people.look: A statuesque figure with pale ice-blue eyes, asymmetric crown-horns and warp-etched skin, and a burn-mark from an old forge spark. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Maqu
people.title: prophet
people.look: A stocky figure with amber eyes, swept obsidian horns and ember-lit eyes, and a burn-mark from an old forge spark. Carries a tablet of prophecies and gestures animatedly while speaking.

people.name: Gassolia
people.title: Imperator of Madqilia
people.look: A sinewy figure with bright gold eyes, raven hair pinned with leaf-filigree, and a silver-stitched scar at the collarbone. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Kenfes
people.title: prophet
people.look: A graceful figure with hazel eyes, raven hair pinned with leaf-filigree, and sharp cheekbones and a crooked nose. Carries a staff hung with scripture-strips and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Yatowuwa
people.title: prophet
people.look: A heavy-set figure with slate-grey eyes, turquoise dewlap frills and turquoise temple-paint, and freckled skin and a wry half-smile. Carries a tablet of prophecies and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Tonkunwin
people.title: hero
people.look: A heavy-set figure with copper-flecked eyes, ridged crocodile brow-scales and jade plugs, and calloused hands stained with ink and oil. Carries a notched masterwork blade and squints thoughtfully before every reply.

people.name: Qanpupjika
people.title: prophet
people.look: A sinewy figure with copper-flecked eyes, braided starlight hair and high pointed ears, and a silver-stitched scar at the collarbone. Carries a tablet of prophecies and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Aringuka
people.title: prophet
people.look: A compact and muscular figure with dark obsidian eyes, sleek brindled fur and ascarred snout, and a faded duelling scar across the cheek. Carries a tablet of prophecies and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Qismiq
people.title: hero
people.look: A lithe figure with pale ice-blue eyes, ringed dreads, and freckled skin and a wry half-smile. Carries a trophy-clasp from a slain beast and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Tanken
people.title: prophet
people.look: A statuesque figure with pale ice-blue eyes, side-whiskers and laugh-lines around bright eyes, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries a staff hung with scripture-strips and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Potali
people.title: prophet
people.look: A wiry figure with bright gold eyes, iridescent crest-scales and slit gold pupils, and sun-creased eyes and a steady gaze. Carries ash-streaked robes and a铜 bell and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Itivigup
people.title: prophet
people.look: A weather-beaten figure with slate-grey eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and sun-creased eyes and a steady gaze. Carries a tablet of prophecies and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Liri
people.title: hero
people.look: A wiry figure with pale ice-blue eyes, swept obsidian horns and ember-lit eyes, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries a trophy-clasp from a slain beast and squints thoughtfully before every reply.

people.name: Ulapusa
people.title: hero
people.look: A compact and muscular figure with amber eyes, sleek brindled fur and ascarred snout, and freckled skin and a wry half-smile. Carries a notched masterwork blade and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Loshuti
people.title: hero

people.name: Liso

people.look: A lean-jawed figure with pale ice-blue eyes, sleek brindled fur and ascarred snout, and a silver-stitched scar at the collarbone. Carries a trophy-clasp from a slain beast and gestures animatedly while speaking.

people.name: Nowa
people.title: Mansa of Daseruku
people.look: A graceful figure with slate-grey eyes, sleek brindled fur and ascarred snout, and stern, deeply etched brow lines. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Apaqing
people.title: Angakkuq of Apinaltuq
people.look: A statuesque figure with pale ice-blue eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and pierced ears hung with small river-pearls. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Apig
people.title: Angakkuq of Iralurimujir
people.look: A stocky figure with copper-flecked eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Anguvumava
people.title: Angakkuq of Itupus
people.look: A sinewy figure with sea-green eyes, sleek brindled fur and ascarred snout, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries a signet ring of state and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Luvulipu
people.title: Angakkuq of Kisipivanu
people.look: A lean-jawed figure with pale ice-blue eyes, wide bat-like ears pierced with brass gears, and sharp cheekbones and a crooked nose. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Suu
people.title: Emperor of Wouzhou
people.look: A tall and gaunt figure with pale ice-blue eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and a faded duelling scar across the cheek. Carries a signet ring of state and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Suu
people.title: Emperor of Luu
people.look: A statuesque figure with copper-flecked eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and a burn-mark from an old forge spark. Carries a signet ring of state and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Khoa
people.title: Emperor of Wuoxia
people.look: A broad-shouldered figure with amber eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and a silver-stitched scar at the collarbone. Carries a signet ring of state and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Shimesi
people.title: Maharaja of Mupadivarta
people.look: A sinewy figure with copper-flecked eyes, glossy iridescent mandibles and compound facets, and sharp cheekbones and a crooked nose. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Uqupum
people.title: hero
people.look: A tall and gaunt figure with deep violet eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and a faded duelling scar across the cheek. Carries a notched masterwork blade and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Ijup
people.title: Angakkuq of Apinaltuq
people.look: A weather-beaten figure with bright gold eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and sharp cheekbones and a crooked nose. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

Houses of the Hospitallers of Light of Bashrib open in Zhodyash.

Luu throws off the yoke of Wuoxia and declares its independence.

The tiny Free Trading Cities of Ruknij seeks shelter and is peacefully absorbed into Vaqjuq.
A royal wedding joins Zokbayresa of Zhodhin and Vityefpena of Zhodyash; the two realms are united under one crown.

The swarm comes from the dry lands in late summer: every green thing around Nubu is eaten, and the granaries of Gesa cannot fill.
The granaries of Gesa cannot make good what was lost; famine stalks the villages around Nubu.
Yofidoba opens the royal granaries of Gesa; bread is carted to every village and the people bless the crown.
The Umapimtuq Campaign is known as the Great Reckoning among the Mohnepih, and as the Plunder among the Amuqimalavaj.
The Border War of Wuoxia is known as the Rightful War among the Maklak, and as the Unprovoked War among the Qea.
The War of Sohchi is known as the Vindication among the Mohnepih, and as the Aggression among the Jaqangisaja.
Wouzhou overruns the defensive holdfasts of Sue, annexing the town and its fertile environs from Wuoxia.
The walls of Shalinabad crumble under heavy assault! Cohorts of Nantun breach the defenses of Shalinabad's capital, scattering the garrison and sacking the palace.
Return of the Sun: People of Gakaja wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Lisangjuaq.
After a bitter siege, the ramparts of Ruoling give way! Vanguard forces of Wouzhou storm the royal seat of Wuoxia, casting down imperial banners and plundering the state vaults.
Garrisons of Naga storm the ramparts of Nagodekot, driving out the defenders of Shalinabad and hoisting their triumphant colors.
Whale Thanks: Boats of Pakjul are blessed and raced off Pakjul; sailors are toasted ashore.
A catastrophic blow to Shalinabad: legions of Naga overrun the citadel of Tadikinagar, seizing the royal seat and routing the high council.
A victor's peace is forged: after 2 years of campaign in the Wuoxia Succession War, Wouzhou prevail, annexing contested borderlands.
Beaten back from stubborn ramparts, the invasion stalls. The War of the Luu Crown concludes after 1 year as Luu successfully preserve their independence.
Wip'eykat II of Jap'op turns from the old cause toward glory.
Solemn rites echo through Jap'op following the death of Likyula the Blessed Kekwiwnoy (a hunting accident). Wip'eykat is crowned sovereign before the assembled court.
Shude II of Doputishoma takes up the cause of the fortunes of the dynasty.
Mourning envelops Doputishoma: Toshaha the Grasping Yuge dies of poison. The royal scepter passes to Shude, an underage youth of 13 years, under the stewardship of high chancellors.

THE GREAT REFORMATION: In Hipi, Tlimotla nails ninety-five theses condemning clerical indulgence! Proclaiming the Reformed Covenant of Hipi, reformers split from ancient dogma. Riots break out as iconoclasts smash old idols.
Defying the crown of Sohchi, the garrison and civic guilds of Qusiku mutiny! The sovereign High Realm of Qusiku is declared with Puluma at its helm.
Puluma is acclaimed ruler of High Realm of Qusiku.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Free Union of Sohchi dispatches punitive legions to subdue High Realm of Qusiku. The bitter Conquest of Qusiku is underway.

ZEALOT UPRISING: Inspired by divine visions and clerical fury, the faithful of Donzon rise against the secular court of Kosudu! Proclaiming holy mandate, Rintontene consecrates the Sacred Order of Donzon.
Rintontene is acclaimed ruler of Sacred Order of Donzon.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Sacred Order of Kosudu dispatches punitive legions to subdue Sacred Order of Donzon. The bitter Border War of Donzon is underway.

REPUBLICAN REVOLT: Declaring citizen liberty inviolable, the populace of Latlohuacan casts out imperial governors! Renouncing allegiance to Apinaltuq, Wicha proclaims the sovereign Free Commonwealth of Latlohuacan.
Wicha is acclaimed ruler of Free Commonwealth of Latlohuacan.
Sparks from a smithy ignite a fierce firestorm in Tadikinagar, destroying ancient temples and market pavilions.
Gisaja (Master Artisan) stages a grand theatrical masterpiece celebrating freedom in Kivipati.
Nefoba (Grand Champion) sweeps all contenders in the Grand Tourney to ecstatic cheers from thousands in Fesango.
Kudomawa (Grand Champion) bestows glorious sporting renown upon the host realm in the international games in Fesango.
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Tedodu! Wofa seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Grand Duchy of Tedodu!

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Crowds fill the avenues of Fimwom as a mass uprising topples the throne of Principality of Fimwom! The ancient autocracy is abolished, and Rarvitgas proclaims the sovereign Democratic Union of Fimwom!

The Conquest of Miprof is known as the Vindication among the Tensinkun, and as the Aggression among the Zizzutbos.
The Hundred Days War of Apinaltuq is known as the War of Deliverance among the Zezzhezyzav, and as the Years of Ash among the Amuqimalavaj.
The Hundred Days War of Nihwimotlan is known as the Rightful War among the Qilqas, and as the Unprovoked War among the Mohnepih.
The Niktuq Campaign is known as the Reclamation among the Qea, and as the Usurpation among the Maklak.
The Border War of Mupadivarta is known as the Holy Defence among the Ginbun, and as the Heretics' War among the Gohi.
Over the centuries Mebi has worn down on the tongue into Mebe; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Over the centuries Ukatin has worn down on the tongue into Ukachin; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Over the centuries Likitleho has worn down on the tongue into Ligitleho; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Whale Thanks: Boats of Qukigu are blessed and raced off Qukigu; sailors are toasted ashore.
Festival of Fire Leaping: Families in Leystan set out lamps and food for their dead at Miprof.
Envoys from Lellabad and Sayshek exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Beta Qigo and Lakngiq exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Citing border encroachments and bitter territorial grievances, Trade Federation of Madqilia mobilizes its hosts against Kingdom of Nihwimotlan. Banners unfurl for the Invasion of Nihwimotlan.

Ambition stirs in the courts of Theocracy of Wouzhou, which openly claims dominion over Confederation of Wuoxia. The lordship braces as the Conquest of Wuoxia erupts. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Munsankoku rally to Wuoxia's side.
White banners flutter over the war camps. The Invasion of Nihwimotlan ends in mutual exhaustion after less than a year; borders return to former lines.
Hihlamah of Lohyihtohwa turns from the old cause toward the spread of the faith.
A perilous interregnum grips Lohyihtohwa following the heirless death of Denwane (poison). Retainers of House Selihmohtoh storm the assembly and usurp the crown.
Yitlinaha of Nihwimotlan takes up the cause of the safety of the lordship.
Dynastic extinction strikes Nihwimotlan: Sehlih dies heirless (old age). Amid whispers of poison and sword-drawn councils, House Napohtle claims the vacant crown.
Ijup of Apinaltuq comes to the throne bent on a lasting legacy.
INTERREGNUM ABOLITION: Dynastic collapse in Apinaltuq ends centuries of kingship! The people formally abolish the monarchy, establishing the United Provinces of Apinaltuq.
Dua of Wuoxia takes up the cause of wealth.
The death of Khoa Khuozeo (old age) leaves Wuoxia without an acknowledged heir. In the ensuing succession crisis, House Kaukhuakau seizes the high throne amidst palace turmoil.
Apumuja of Apinaltuq takes up the cause of a lasting legacy.
The death of Ijup Ingigungav (old age) leaves Apinaltuq without an acknowledged heir. In the ensuing succession crisis, House Aningut seizes the high throne amidst palace turmoil.

THE GREAT REFORMATION: In Yunzaki, Teto nails ninety-five theses condemning clerical indulgence! Proclaiming the Reformed Covenant of Yunzaki, reformers split from ancient dogma. Riots break out as iconoclasts smash old idols.

REPUBLICAN REVOLT: Declaring citizen liberty inviolable, the populace of Donzon casts out imperial governors! Renouncing allegiance to Nantun, Manginbane proclaims the sovereign Democratic Union of Donzon.
Manginbane is acclaimed ruler of Democratic Union of Donzon.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Stratocracy of Nantun dispatches punitive legions to subdue Democratic Union of Donzon. The bitter Great Nantun War is underway.
Merchant guilds of Mutujuaq open an expansive paved trade highway, linking mountain passes to bustling lowlands.
Lingaji (Archmage) transmutes lead into silver, filling the state coffers in Julu.
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Fufkhat strike at midnight in Lellabad! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Principality of Lellabad!
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Rono strike at midnight in Tedodu! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Trade Federation of Tedodu!
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Wenama strike at midnight in Kosudu! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Sacred Order of Kosudu!
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Gufasu strike at midnight in Daseruku! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Divine Realm of Daseruku!

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Crowds fill the avenues of Refkand as a mass uprising topples the throne of Free Union of Refkand! The ancient autocracy is abolished, and Wangin proclaims the sovereign United Provinces of Refkand!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Iralurimujir are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Gesa!
QUEST COMPLETED: Rescue of the Ice-Stranded Hunters near Vivumiligamu! Jimata brings every hunter back and the camp shares out 100 Gold!
QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Pujsasraja embarks upon the Search for the Winter Cache of Senrof! Pujsasraja hears of an old food and tool cache buried in snow near Senrof.
TITAN CLASH: The armies of Madqilia clash with Drakon the Pyre-Lord in cell 981! The beast resists with 151/340 HP.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Ligitleho pave the Ligitleho-Ki-fafu Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Ligitleho and Ki-fafu (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Ruoling pave the Ruoling-Meucheng Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Ruoling and Meucheng (+trade, +stability).
The Miprof–Tedshahr Maglev is rebuilt: Leystan takes over the line and relays the track, and trains run again.
The Kunshima–Yingan Maglev opens: the first maglev of Tanyinkoku runs from Kunshima to Yingan, with stations in both towns.
The Nametakot–Naki Railway of Ditodi reaches Doputishoma: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).
NATURE BLESSING: Gorath the Stone Peak heaves rich subterranean veins to the surface of Zunrinhara! Granite ramparts harden against all siegecraft (+25 gold, +15 stability).
Yatowuwa, eyes sewn shut, preaches in Motekusoka that the fallen sovereign will return to those who gaze inward.
A bone-masked seer, Itivigup, descends into Amumiqaj and speaks the names of those who will die before spring.
Unrest of the year: bread riots in Maltuq (Wouzhou).

Rono of Tedodu comes to the throne bent on wealth.
Wenama of Kosudu comes to the throne bent on glory.

Tenkenmi of Tanyinkoku lets go of the aim for glory.
Nedgekha conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Frozen Ridge) using tactic (score 9 vs DC 8). Defeated Astra. Promoted to F-Rank!

The Wandering Consort of Fozhgird finds patrons in Gansunwin.
The Ember Players of Hasu finds patrons in Fimwom.
Houses of the Knights of Church of the Raven open in Sayshek.
Delvers of Tedodu break into the bones of an elder wyrm beyond Wikemo; the deep realm grows.
Borne on the winds, Kikmal now drifts above the open sea.
Sayshek squeezes the shaft-tolls of Amat; the miners of Ugikmiut mutter beneath the stone.
Rumngiv squeezes the shaft-tolls of Daseruku; the miners of Daseruku mutter beneath the stone.
U-nokedo squeezes the shaft-tolls of Upumjuaq; the miners of Atununaat mutter beneath the stone.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Julu bars the shaft to Amumiqaj, and the tithe-collectors of Amumiqaj are turned back at the lamps of Qukigu.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Chehsih bars the shaft to Poche, and the tithe-collectors of Poche are turned back at the lamps of Sohchi.

SKY BLOCKADE: the floating hosts of Vaqtuq close the air-lanes above Bisha, starving Bisha of the high trade.

The final citadels fall, and the crown of Confederacy of Ngakjunglin is broken forever. With treasuries emptied and borders dissolved, Luppunrim Sankarkuppav flees into bitter exile as the lordship fades into legend.

monsters.name: Ziz the Storm-Sovereign

monsters.name: The Great Sun Lion

monsters.name: The Red-Fearing Nian

monsters.name: Timingila the Whale-Swallower
monsters.lore: A sea monster of the old epics so vast it swallows whales whole, and is itself swallowed by something larger still.

monsters.name: Smokeless-Fire Ifrit
monsters.lore: A spirit of smokeless fire, proud and cunning, bound by old seals and older bargains.

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards

people.name: Mintirsos
people.title: hero
people.look: A lean-jawed figure with deep violet eyes, swept obsidian horns and ember-lit eyes, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries a trophy-clasp from a slain beast and gestures animatedly while speaking.

people.name: Naddula
people.title: hero
people.look: A stocky figure with bright gold eyes, asymmetric crown-horns and warp-etched skin, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries a notched masterwork blade and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Rolngong
people.title: prophet
people.look: A statuesque figure with amber eyes, swept obsidian horns and ember-lit eyes, and pierced ears hung with small river-pearls. Carries a tablet of prophecies and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Kiku
people.title: Jarl of Setia
people.look: A broad-shouldered figure with copper-flecked eyes, desiccated royal wrappings and a gilded death-mask, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Can
people.title: artist
people.look: A stocky figure with slate-grey eyes, void-dyed braids set with a glowing spirit-stone, and freckled skin and a wry half-smile. Carries a case of pigments and silverpoint styluses and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Lutspala
people.title: hero
people.look: A lean-jawed figure with deep violet eyes, a soot-darkened beard clasped with rune-iron, and sun-creased eyes and a steady gaze. Carries a notched masterwork blade and gestures animatedly while speaking.

people.name: Tsutszosha
people.title: hero
people.look: A sinewy figure with amber eyes, a soot-darkened beard clasped with rune-iron, and sharp cheekbones and a crooked nose. Carries a notched masterwork blade and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Nung
people.title: inventor
people.look: A tall and gaunt figure with copper-flecked eyes, void-dyed braids set with a glowing spirit-stone, and calloused hands stained with ink and oil. Carries a ticking clockwork gizmo and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

people.title: Sapa Inca of Chutpampa
people.look: A weather-beaten figure with sea-green eyes, wide bat-like ears pierced with brass gears, and sun-creased eyes and a steady gaze. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Nilu
people.title: Shah of Ranezho
people.look: A stocky figure with storm-grey eyes, wind-tangled curls, and freckled skin and a wry half-smile. Carries a signet ring of state and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

people.name: Nazsaza
people.title: hero
people.look: A sinewy figure with dark obsidian eyes, chitinous cranial crest and twitching antennae, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries a notched masterwork blade and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

people.name: Døhdmab
people.title: hero
people.look: A stocky figure with copper-flecked eyes, a soot-darkened beard clasped with rune-iron, and a burn-mark from an old forge spark. Carries a notched masterwork blade and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

people.name: Nope
people.title: Oba of Motimowesogo
people.look: A tall and gaunt figure with hazel eyes, long tusks andriver-pebble dermal ridges, and a faded duelling scar across the cheek. Carries a signet ring of state and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Wuchkara
people.title: Sapa Inca of Palchippap
people.look: A sinewy figure with bright gold eyes, wide bat-like ears pierced with brass gears, and sun-creased eyes and a steady gaze. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Zakheta
people.title: Shah of Dadogird
people.look: A heavy-set figure with hazel eyes, silver-streaked temples, and stern, deeply etched brow lines. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Qutrach
people.title: Sapa Inca of HihTawantin
people.look: A broad-shouldered figure with sea-green eyes, a sharp grin and soot-smudged goggles on the forehead, and a silver-stitched scar at the collarbone. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and gestures animatedly while speaking.

people.name: Lipchata
people.title: Sapa Inca of Hiptursuyu
people.look: A lithe figure with bright gold eyes, wide bat-like ears pierced with brass gears, and a faded duelling scar across the cheek. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Tukliqtila
people.title: Sapa Inca of Hiptursuyu
people.look: A graceful figure with hazel eyes, a sharp grin and soot-smudged goggles on the forehead, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries a signet ring of state and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Fely
people.title: Jarl of Lythipømu
people.look: A heavy-set figure with dark obsidian eyes, desiccated royal wrappings and a gilded death-mask, and sun-creased eyes and a steady gaze. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and gestures animatedly while speaking.

events.text: Masquerade Season: People of Motimowesogo wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Monidan.
The walls of Sothe crumble under heavy assault! Cohorts of Nelgondar breach the defenses of Pylumark's capital, scattering the garrison and sacking the palace.
The sun sets upon Democratic Union of Pylumark. Bereft of armies and abandoned by vassals, the lordship collapses into history; Tha Mififøly escapes into the wilderness.
The Conquest of Pylumark reaches its conclusion after 2 years of bloodshed: Nelgondar triumph decisively, forcing a humiliating treaty upon their foes.
Feast of Breaking the Fast: Bonfires on the hills of Qasr Qajdad greet the high sun above Qasr Qajdad.
Feast of the Pilgrim Caravan: Granaries of Shaqtiy Beyond are opened at Qashsiy; the whole town eats until dusk.
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the Qisyashabad Campaign after 2 years. With frontiers redrawn, Shaqtiy dictate terms to the vanquished.
Humbled, Principality of Qisyashabad bends the knee and becomes a vassal of Shaqtiy, paying yearly tribute.
Talhakhana of Nihwiwpata turns from the old cause toward wealth.
A perilous interregnum grips Nihwiwpata following the heirless death of Hakluh (old age). Retainers of House Chikhihnul storm the assembly and usurp the crown.
Masons in Dosyleky lay the final battlements upon monumental stone walls encircling Gøgepøny, fortifying the jewel of the lordship.
Yiba (Grand Champion) defeats a formidable foreign knight in single combat before the royal court in Fuvågø.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Agitators dispatched by Shaqtiy Beyond stir mutiny among garrison troops in Tsofchallih!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Shaqtiy Beyond are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Tsofchallih!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Covert saboteurs from Lasboch detonate powder stores in Siteni Beyond, gutting frontline regiments!

Soldiers scatter the marchers of the Friends of the People in Thiby; the demand for enfranchisement is drowned in blood.
The cause of emancipation spreads through the towns of Sabitishesi Beyond; pamphlets and sermons decry thralldom.
Waves of Kinhunwin folk, fleeing turmoil, cross from Suntunkawa and settle the borderlands of Surafistan.
Ranezho squeezes the shaft-tolls of Binọ; the miners of Sugama mutter beneath the stone.
Ranezho squeezes the shaft-tolls of Balmir; the miners of Paftal mutter beneath the stone.
The spring flood of the Retø is the worst in living memory: Gira is cut off for a month.
The Qisyashabad Campaign is known as the Vindication in Shaqtiy, and as the Aggression in Qisyashabad.
Burning of Winter: People of Gubia wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Chobrab.
Feast of Lights: The longest night in Sebdar is spent by firelight in Sebdar, with stories and gifts.
Midsummer Bonfires: Bonfires on the hills of Durn greet the high sun above Durn.
Winter Nights: Families in Hitegy set out lamps and food for their dead at Dosugo.
Old border feuds boil over into open bloodshed: Commercial Union of Gihamark launches a determined invasion into Chiefdom of Tsitspibdoz, igniting the Gihamark–Tsitspibdoz War.
White banners flutter over the war camps. The Gihamark–Tsitspibdoz War ends in mutual exhaustion after less than a year; borders return to former lines.
Sothatguga of Tsitspibdoz turns from the old cause toward glory.
In the royal halls of Tsitspibdoz, Shurgug the Great Tsigtsin breathes their last, succumbing to fever. Sothatguga ascends the ancestral throne amid solemn acclamation.

REPUBLICAN REVOLT: Weary of monarchical tyranny, the burghers and civic guilds of Dishziymid take up arms for freedom! Seceding from Finkhing, they hoist republican banners beneath Tanyumsima to establish the Free Commonwealth of Dishziymid.
Tanyumsima is acclaimed ruler of Free Commonwealth of Dishziymid.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Commercial Union of Finkhing dispatches punitive legions to subdue Free Commonwealth of Dishziymid. The bitter Great Finkhing War is underway.
Defying the crown of Sugama, the garrison and civic guilds of Oyo-rese mutiny! The sovereign Grand Marshalate of Oyo-rese is declared with Nofa at its helm.
Nofa is acclaimed ruler of Grand Marshalate of Oyo-rese.

Outraged by treason, the crown of Polytechnic League of Sugama mobilizes imperial cohorts to crush the upstart insurrection in Grand Marshalate of Oyo-rese. The Invasion of Oyo-rese begins in fire and iron.
A brief gilded dusk settles over Lasboch: cathedral bells ring clear, the plague wanes and the old glory seems near.
Master Artificer Nung of Qungwuzhou achieves worldwide acclaim with their magnum opus: "The Compound Lever Crane".

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Spurred by cries for liberty and bread, popular assemblies across Hunmunzaki overthrow the old order! Monarchy is dismantled, and the revolutionary convention inaugurates the Popular Commonwealth of Hunmunzaki.
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Nelgondar! Hyna seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Iron Dominion of Nelgondar!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Ralezamin are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Qisyashabad!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Qasr Qajdad are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Kadigu!

Tsutszosha, a lone hunter, stalks the beast-infested wards of Bibrad through three nights of mist and ends it.
The Choir of the Hollow Crown marks the doors of Shari with a cracked eye; those who see it do not sleep.

Quknap of Nihwiwpata turns from the old cause toward a lasting legacy.
Dynastic extinction strikes Nihwiwpata: Talhakhana dies heirless (a hunting accident). Amid whispers of poison and sword-drawn councils, House Pinnich claims the vacant crown.

The World Congress ratified 'Edict on the Prohibition of Dread Sorcery', outlawing catastrophic dark sorcery across all civilized borders.
The World Congress enacted 'Charter of Free Navigation and Open Seas', opening global maritime sea lanes and granting +20% international trade wealth.
Hitegy stands condemned as a rogue state in defiance of World Congress law, suffering trade embargoes.
Finkhing stands condemned as a rogue state in defiance of World Congress law, suffering trade embargoes.
Dyftal stands condemned as a rogue state in defiance of World Congress law, suffering trade embargoes.

Furs and amber from Balbig reach the great fair at Balmir.
Merchants on the route between Setia and Nufrin settle on the Kinhunwin tongue as their lingua franca.
The old commons no longer suffice for so wide a realm as Shashahr; it turns to free guilds.
Delvers of Chutpampa break into a vast geode cavern; the deep realm grows.
Over 84 years the speech of Surafistan has drifted from the Danuhuto tongue; its people now call themselves the Sebmiy.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Pisbyp bars the shaft to Gohona, and the tithe-collectors of Ralezamin are turned back at the lamps of Paftal.
Bub squeezes the shaft-tolls of Rupbamba; the miners of Hiptursuyu mutter beneath the stone.
SKY BLOCKADE: the floating hosts of Sonkoku close the air-lanes above Mansun, starving Hunmunzaki of the high trade.

The War of the Bozwesduk Crown is known as the War of Deliverance among the Suri, and as the Years of Ash among the Zewshamsar.
The Paftal–Balbig War is known as the Great Reckoning in Paftal, and as the Plunder in Balbig.
Over the centuries Teyngotnagara has worn down on the tongue into Cheyngotnagara; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Over the centuries Sorohadu has worn down on the tongue into Soroadu; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Over the centuries Kenkawa has worn down on the tongue into Kenkaw; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Water Festival: People of Gegdid wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Gegdid.
Feast of New Light: People of Zhushi wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Vagama.
Denouncing ancient covenants, the heralds of Artificer Directorate of Shaqtiy proclaim war upon Principality of Hitegy. Trumpets sound across the frontier as the Conquest of Hitegy begins.

Citing border encroachments and bitter territorial grievances, Realm of Davirike mobilizes its hosts against Syndicate of Paftal. Banners unfurl for the Invasion of Paftal. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Sugama rally to Paftal's side.
White banners flutter over the war camps. The Conquest of Hitegy ends in mutual exhaustion after less than a year; borders return to former lines.

Galled by heavy ichor-tithes and distant decrees, the citizens of Oyo-rese cast out their ward-wardens! Renouncing all allegiance to Sugama, Nofa proclaims the sovereign Council of Ingenuity of Oyo-rese.
Nofa is acclaimed ruler of Council of Ingenuity of Oyo-rese.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Artificer Directorate of Sugama dispatches punitive legions to subdue Council of Ingenuity of Oyo-rese. The bitter War of Sugama is underway.
Flames sweep unimpeded through Oyo-rese; hundreds flee into the streets as bucket brigades battle the raging conflagration.
Grand Champion Renkhupia of Qurlukh achieves worldwide acclaim with their magnum opus: "Victor of the Colosseum".
Gannon (Grand Champion) sets an unprecedented record in the sprint and javelin throwing trials in Rongdu.
Can (Master Artisan) composes an immortal ballad that brings tears to commoners and kings alike in Henyen.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Counterfeit letters planted by Shaqtiy rupture trust between Bub and their ally Chodsk!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Shaqtiy are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Bub!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Hiptursuyu are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Oyo-rese!

ARCANE MELTDOWN: Unstable alchemy and runaway leyline containment experiments detonate violently near Arcane Proving Grounds of Cell 1692! Magical shockwaves scorch the earth into irradiated ash, collapsing towers and displacing hundreds.
QUEST COMPLETED: Reopening the Collapsed Rock Church of Nelgondar! Kagdek sees the doors open before the feast and the chanting begins, winning Immortal Renown and a steadier realm!
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Bopakand pave the Bopakand-Sugama Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Bopakand and Sugama (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Siteni Beyond pave the Melgard-Sonwenmoto Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Melgard and Sonwenmoto (+trade, +stability).
ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Shubbog the Brood Mother spawns thousands of chittering dark young in the sacred groves of Finkhing, swarming forward under black skies (+20% army power, -6 stability).
Unrest of the year: sectarian clashes in Fukhastan (HihTawantin).

monsters.name: Lion of the Golden Dawn
monsters.lore: An immortal noble lion with a mane of radiant sunlight, whose majestic roar dispels dark enchantments.
monsters.trophy: Solar Lion Mane of Golden Light

monsters.name: The Eclipse Wolf
monsters.lore: A terrifying dread wolf of midnight taigas, capable of swallowing whole warbands beneath the winter moon.

monsters.name: Brimstone the Dragon-King
monsters.lore: An ancient volcanic dragon sleeping atop mountains of melted gold, reducing invading armies to calcined bones.

monsters.name: White Tiger of the Ridge
monsters.lore: A colossal pale tiger of snow-clad ridges, silent as autumn wind, that warbands speak of only in whispers.

monsters.name: Roc the Sky-Render
monsters.lore: The roc of sailors' and caravaneers' tall tales, a bird vast enough to carry off an elephant; its wingbeats raise dust storms over the canyons.

monsters.name: Titan of the Steppes
monsters.lore: A colossal terrestrial colossus whose bones are tubes of bronze and limbs like bars of iron, roaming ancient grasslands.

monsters.name: Glacies the Glacial Drake
monsters.lore: A frost-breathing great wyrm dwelling in glacial crevasses, freezing rivers solid with a single exhalation.

monsters.name: Kraken the Fleet-Devourer
monsters.lore: A colossal multi-tentacled sea monster capable of pulling entire armadas down into the black abyss.

monsters.name: The River Kappa
monsters.lore: A water imp with a dish of water on its head; bow to it, and courtesy forces it to bow back and spill its strength.

monsters.name: The Basilisk of the Ruins
monsters.lore: A crowned serpent whose gaze turns the living to stone; only a mirror or a weasel defeats it.

monsters.name: Nian the New-Year Beast
monsters.lore: A horned beast that comes down from the mountains each new year, driven off only by red banners and firecrackers.

monsters.name: Smokeless-Fire Ifrit
monsters.lore: A spirit of smokeless fire, proud and cunning, bound by old seals and older bargains.

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards

events.text: NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Nacarona pave the Qica-Velici Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Qica and Velici (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Debre Chesuro pave the Debre Chesuro-Qemaruqo Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Debre Chesuro and Qemaruqo (+trade, +stability).
The Wu'sopu–Ne'bu Maglev of Wo'nuckab reaches E'nik'in: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).
The Pliglo–Freprona Maglev opens: another maglev of Betakopege runs from Pliglo to Freprona, with stations in both towns.
RUINOUS GIFT: Luxuria the Gilded Prince intoxicates the high courts of Motadugu with exquisite hedonism! Opulence surges alongside reckless decadence (+40 gold, -10 stability).
The pilgrim granaries of Morced stand empty while the lords of Bobmagsmow feast; the hungry batter at the chapter-house doors.
The Order of the Cracked Eye marks the doors of Caer Rob with a cracked eye; those who see it do not sleep.
Sasvuyhid, eyes sewn shut, preaches in Duddosh that the fallen sovereign will return to those who gaze inward.
The Ashen Chapter gathers in the catacombs beneath Vale, whispering of the sight that lies past the veil.
Unrest of the year: tax riots in Tukkukyeh (Rutkyyxar); tax riots in Fraflu.

Heta of Mihemi secures the line, with Vapuli grown to take the crown.
Donyidi conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Gilded Vault) using tactic (score 25 vs DC 8). Defeated Vorgar. Promoted to F-Rank!
Kiwarome survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 7 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red. Salvaged ancient relic: Sun Stone Shard!
The court of Nacarona bans the Lantern Circle of Qukifu; its masters flee across the border.
A schism divides the Barefoot Friars of Mysteries of Fisulefune: the houses of Nacarona follow a stricter rule as the Reformed Barefoot Friars of Mysteries of Fisulefune.
Houses of the Lore-Wardens of Path of Slerlu open in Kanoge.
In Laforo the Friends of the People gathers crowds behind Pifelu Vifivu, demanding enfranchisement for Laforo.
Whispers in the fields of Fuhokand: a movement of free tenants gathers the tenants against manorial fiefs.
Something vast stirs in the lightless depths beneath Fuhokand; the deep wardens double their watch.
SKY BLOCKADE: the floating hosts of Hunmunzaki Beyond close the air-lanes above Ki-dogano, starving Bobodo of the high trade.
The swarm comes from the dry lands in late summer: every green thing around E'pojuha is eaten, and the granaries of Ziuling cannot fill.
A victor's peace is forged: after 1 year of campaign in the Hundred Days War of Diytocpatna, Vishdesh prevail, annexing contested borderlands.
Hunmunzaki Beyond's invasion through the Burning Veil into Pongpen was repulsed at Nircofnum.
Mihevu marches an army across the Singing Gate into Sirati, storming Yontun!
Dance of the Elders: Families in Bobodo set out lamps and food for their dead at Datudu.
Envoys from Bobmagsmow and Khevapigird exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Old border feuds boil over into open bloodshed: Free City of Fuhokand launches a determined invasion into Democratic Union of Pahmo, igniting the Great Fuhokand War.
Exhausted by protracted attrition, both sides sign an armistice concluding the Great Fuhokand War (less than a year). Scabbards are sheathed and the status quo ante is restored.
Defying the crown of Shictevarta, the garrison and civic guilds of Toccimpura mutiny! The sovereign Artificer Directorate of Toccimpura is declared with Bashyindon at its helm.
Bashyindon is acclaimed ruler of Artificer Directorate of Toccimpura.
Vowing to eradicate rebellion, Trade Federation of Shictevarta marches swiftly upon Artificer Directorate of Toccimpura. The drums of the Toccimpura Succession War echo across the provinces.

AGRARIAN REVOLT: Crushed by feudal ichor-tithes and noble exploitation, the laborers of Diytocpatna rise in open insurrection! Renouncing the lords of Vishdesh, they establish the Free Union of Diytocpatna with Dovshosh leading the commune.
Dovshosh is acclaimed ruler of Free Union of Diytocpatna.

REPUBLICAN REVOLT: Weary of monarchical tyranny, the burghers and civic guilds of Tanafu take up arms for freedom! Seceding from Lyvkud, they hoist republican banners beneath Tara to establish the United Provinces of Tanafu.
Tara is acclaimed ruler of United Provinces of Tanafu.
The Great Plague comes to E'nipekab. Doors are marked, carts of the dead roll at night, and E'nipekab trembles.
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Zovapaba storm the government palace in Wo'jinajaw! The faction seizes control, establishing the Grand Duchy of Wo'jinajaw.

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Crowds fill the avenues of Bludlu as a mass uprising topples the throne of Confederation of Bludlu! The ancient autocracy is abolished, and Tumu proclaims the sovereign Workers' Federation of Bludlu!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Counterfeit letters planted by Vulibufo rupture trust between Biwiwa and their ally Al-sha!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Hochehla are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Bobotu!
HUNT IN PROGRESS: Tola duels Lion of the Golden Dawn! The titan endures with 130/230 HP.
QUEST COMPLETED: Retrieval of the Whispering Tome of Puwe! Ryqqirraxa seals the tome in lead and brings out the relic, winning the sacred relic Astral Capacitor of Slatraqlu!
QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Tubaqa embarks upon the Recovery of the Illuminated Book of Gøthmåm! Tubaqa learns of an illuminated book hidden in a cave monastery near Gøthmåm during an old war.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Toccimpura pave the Toccimpura-Fenaba Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Toccimpura and Fenaba (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Khevapigird pave the Khevapigird-Bludlu Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Khevapigird and Bludlu (+trade, +stability).
The Qaqeruqo–Duddosh Maglev opens: the first maglev of Qaqeruqo runs from Qaqeruqo to Duddosh, with stations in both towns.

DIVINE PROXY WAR: The war between Shictevarta and Toccimpura escalates into a celestial proxy duel! Luxuria the Gilded Prince rallies the hosts of Shictevarta, while Ignis the Hearth Caldera unleashes sacred omens to shield Toccimpura.
RUINOUS GIFT: Luxuria the Gilded Prince intoxicates the high courts of Shictevarta with exquisite hedonism! Opulence surges alongside reckless decadence (+40 gold, -10 stability).
NATURE BLESSING: Ignis the Hearth Caldera stokes the caldera hearths of Toccimpura! Master smiths forge shimmering obsidian weaponry bathed in magma (+16% army power, +15 gold).

The War of Zhapebo is known as the Reclamation among the Khafipo, and as the Usurpation among the Qigugisuqi.
The War of the Shehman Crown is known as the Vindication in Shehman, and as the Aggression in Toshpatna.
The Hundred Days War of Rutavu is known as the Liberation among the Trabrukhri, and as the Betrayal among the Qigugisuqi.
Over the centuries Tu'pupejosu has worn down on the tongue into Tu'pupejos; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Over the centuries Rerowetevifi has worn down on the tongue into Rerwetevifi; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Over the centuries Kuzhofahe has worn down on the tongue into Kuzhofah; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Feast of First Fruits: Granaries of Rodelowedara are opened at Rodelowedara; the whole town eats until dusk.

Citing border encroachments and bitter territorial grievances, Protectorate of Betakopege mobilizes its hosts against Principality of Pehnihtlan. Banners unfurl for the War of Betakopege. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Bludlu rally to Pehnihtlan's side.
Ambition stirs in the courts of Rift-Dominion of Nantun, which openly claims dominion over Free Union of Morihinui. The lordship braces as the Hundred Days War of Morihinui erupts.
Ghi'axqeiz of Ghoerugg takes up the cause of the fortunes of the dynasty.
Solemn rites echo through Ghoerugg following the death of Ghi'axiix Stormborn Ki'aghyok (poison). Ghi'axqeiz is crowned sovereign before the assembled court.
Zanasi of Biwiwa comes to the throne bent on wealth.
Solemn rites echo through Biwiwa following the death of Runima II the Tall Samisha (battle wounds). Zanasi is crowned sovereign before the assembled court.
Tolre' of Xaqlit takes up the cause of glory.
The bells of Xaqlit toll for the passing of Ratquqa II Longspear Yolxu'qiq (a hunting accident). The youth Tolre' ascends the throne under a regency council.
QUEST COMPLETED: Delve into the Primeval Foundry in Nutiyya! Hitewungu returns triumphant from Nutiyya, having uncovered forgotten secrets and winning Immortal Renown!
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Ni'simomipi pave the Jope-Ghoerriogh Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Jope and Ghoerriogh (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Rodelowedara pave the Lorotu-Kuzhofah Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Lorotu and Kuzhofah (+trade, +stability).
The Hetkot–Toshpatna Maglev is rebuilt: Shehman takes over the line and relays the track, and trains run again.
The Caer Mol–Moldyw Maglev opens: another maglev of Bobmagsmow runs from Caer Mol to Moldyw, with stations in both towns.

ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Cthulor the Abyssal Slumberer stirs in the ocean abyss beneath Pu'chajaw! Barnacle-encrusted cyclopean monoliths surface, loaded with pre-human treasure (+35 gold, -5 stability).
NATURE BLESSING: Undina of the Silver Basin purifies the sacred rivers of Ghoerugg! Abundant fish and unhindered river trade enrich the townships (+30 gold, +12 stability).
NATURE BLESSING: Sylvanor the Forest Horn awakens the ancient canopies of Toshpatna! Verdant thickets ensnare enemies and provide abundant woodland forage (+16 stability, +10% army power).
Unrest of the year: tax riots in Rencyls (Bobmagsmow).

Kozhaza of Khoka lets go of the aim for a lasting legacy.
Muva of Riwamu sets down the scholar's pursuits.
Lotasa of Fisita keeps the lordship whole through 20 hard years.
Fassutqaka conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Gilded Vault) using assault (score 19 vs DC 8). Defeated Vorgar. Promoted to F-Rank!
Qepakha survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 6 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red. Salvaged ancient relic: Sun Stone Shard!
In the lands Ziuling won by the sword, 9 districts now speak the See tongue and keep its customs.
Houses of the Reformed Barefoot Friars of Mysteries of Fisulefune open in Qemaruqo.
Kofa of Ranutenui yields to the Commons Assembly: enfranchisement becomes the law of the land.
Pevevaka Venuruhu founds the Tillers Union in Pafutika; its pamphlets call for land reform across Perirupi.
Ledvud Bolduv founds the League of the Clear Cup in Vagaluzu; its pamphlets call for temperance across Toshpatna.
Dav mac Dolmobced founds the Charter League in Mordod; its pamphlets call for legal reform across Lylia.
Delvers of Dine break into a hall of glowing crystals; the deep realm grows.
The tiny Popular Commonwealth of Vacium seeks shelter and is peacefully absorbed into Bobmagsmow.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Khastan bars the shaft to Fane, and the tithe-collectors of Mibodeba are turned back at the lamps of Ghoerugg.
The flood-silt of the Khofu makes the bottomlands of Viawuhe the greenest in Perirupi.

monsters.name: Brimstone the Dragon-King
monsters.lore: An ancient volcanic dragon sleeping atop mountains of melted gold, reducing invading armies to calcined bones.

monsters.name: Ziz the Storm-Sovereign
monsters.lore: A colossal winged terror of celestial heights whose wingspan eclipses the noon sun and commands cyclones.

monsters.name: Titan of the Steppes
monsters.lore: A colossal terrestrial colossus whose bones are tubes of bronze and limbs like bars of iron, roaming ancient grasslands.

monsters.name: The Storm Roc of the Badlands
monsters.lore: The roc of sailors' and caravaneers' tall tales, a bird vast enough to carry off an elephant; its wingbeats raise dust storms over the canyons.

monsters.name: Tusk-Lord of the Briars
monsters.lore: A massive armored tusker leading wild forest herds, tearing up farmland and trampling watchtowers.
monsters.trophy: Calydonian Boar Great Tusks & Armored Hide

monsters.name: The Emerald Qilin
monsters.lore: A gentle horned dragon-beast cloaked in scales of jade, appearing only during the reigns of benevolent and enlightened rulers.

monsters.name: Lion of the Golden Dawn
monsters.lore: An immortal noble lion with a mane of radiant sunlight, whose majestic roar dispels dark enchantments.
monsters.trophy: Solar Lion Mane of Golden Light

monsters.name: Shadow of the Loch
monsters.lore: An elusive plesiosaur-like lake cryptid spoken of in local campfire folklore, surfacing only when mists veil the waters.

monsters.name: The Forest Sasabonsam
monsters.lore: A long-legged forest being that dangles from the canopy to snatch the careless traveller.

monsters.name: The Bakunawa of the Lake
monsters.lore: A great sea serpent that rises to swallow the moon; villagers drive it back by banging pots and pans until it spits the moon out.

monsters.name: Draugr of the Howe
monsters.lore: An undead warrior who guards the treasure of its burial mound, growing heavier than an ox.

monsters.name: The Red-Fearing Nian
monsters.lore: A horned beast that comes down from the mountains each new year, driven off only by red banners and firecrackers.

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards
